summary.text: Mark Nair is the Democratic nominee challenging incumbent Ronny Jackson in Texas's 13th District. A former Amarillo city councilman, he describes himself as an inventor, entrepreneur and educator who worked for more than two decades at an entertainment-distribution company before teaching economics and software development at Amarillo College. His campaign focuses on healthcare, government accountability and education.

paragraphs.text: Nair earned a high school diploma from Westfield High School, a bachelor's degree from Texas A&M University in 1988 and a graduate degree from Texas A&M in 1991.

In his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, he says he worked for 23 years in the entertainment distribution business at Anderson Merchandisers; his campaign website says he was the company's head of innovation.
He has taught economics and software development at the college level, and he says he won the Faculty Excellence Award at Amarillo College in 2020.

Nair describes himself as an inventor with a few technological patents and a member of the National Academy of Inventors, and says he helps mentor startup companies at the Texas Tech Innovation Hub and the National Science Foundation.
He is a former member of the Amarillo City Council.
Nair ran unopposed in the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary and received 28,198 votes.
Nair has lived in Amarillo for more than 30 years with his wife, Suzanne; he says they have three children, all born in Amarillo.
